turns.t: Morning. Come for the stroke review.
Good morning, Mr Hale. It's three months since your stroke. How's the physio going?
Good. Walking better. Hand's slower.
Which hand?
Right. Can't do buttons yet.
Any new weakness, numbness, or speech problems?
No. None.
Any falls, or near-falls?
No falls.
Good. Let me see you do some things. Squeeze my fingers. ~
Like this?
Good grip, a bit weaker on the right than the left, but better than last time.
Is that good? ~
It's improving. Now walk to the door and back, and then touch your nose with your right finger. ~
Right.
A slightly slow, careful gait with a mild drag of the right foot, steady, no stumbling. ~
I've been doing the exercises. ~
It shows. Have you started anything new, a new activity, or driving? ~
Not driving. Doctor said no. ~
Correct. Sensible. And how are you managing at home?
I live with my daughter. She helps.
Your operation was on your neck, wasn't it, your carotid artery?
Yes. The left. Before the stroke. A year ago.
Right. The surgeon wanted a scan of that side, to check it's staying open, so I'd like to arrange a carotid ultrasound.
When? ~
Within a month. The hospital will write. ~
Fine. ~
Keep up the exercises, and the hand ones are important, with putty or buttons or coins.
Buttons. Yes. ~
And if you notice a sudden weakness, a drooping face, slurred speech, call 999 immediately, don't wait.
I know. FAST. ~
Exactly. Well done for working so hard. ~
Thank you. ~
